summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and a history of dialysis access complications was admitted for worsening hand ischemia due to steal syndrome from her right upper extremity AV fistula. She underwent successful fistula banding to reduce blood flow and restore perfusion to her hand. Postoperatively, she was monitored for pain, circulation, and anticoagulation management, with warfarin held temporarily and restarted the following day. She received scheduled hemodialysis during admission with stable recovery, no complications, and resolution of ischemic symptoms. She was discharged home with instructions on wound care, activity restrictions, medications including short-term pain control and stool softener, and follow-up with the surgical team in two weeks.
